Harishchandra Hore.description: Manager of Nirupama Hotel, a responsible and alert man in his mid-forties who discovers the murder.

Gunadhar.description: Uniformed bearer at Nirupama Hotel, efficient and attentive to the guests' needs.

Byomkesh Bakshi.description: The famous detective, known as the Truth Seeker, who investigates the murder at Nirupama Hotel.

Rakhal Sarkar.description: The police inspector in charge of the murder case and a friend of Byomkesh Bakshi, often referred to simply as Sarkar.

Shachitosh Sanyal.description: Boarder in Room Number Three, unwell during the events, questioned by police.

Dr. Shobhona Roy.description: Dr. Shobhona Roy is a lady doctor staying in Room Number One at Nirupama Hotel, later revealed as the mother-in-law of the victim, and sometimes referred to as Dr. Roy.

Rampirit Singh.description: The Bhojpuri gatekeeper of Nirupama Hotel, nicknamed General Singh for his military-like appearance.

Sukanto Som.description: A former filmstar turned blackmailer who was murdered while staying at the Nirupama Hotel under the alias Rajkumar Basu.

Bhagaban Mohanti.description: A hardened criminal and fugitive who appears in the victim's diary under the alias Jagabandhu Patra.

Mohanlal Kumar.description: A person listed in the diary, absent during the investigation.

Shyamakanta Lahiri.description: Another person listed in the diary, works in the Port Commissioner's office.

Latika Choudhury.description: A woman blackmailed by Sukanto Som, with a past romantic involvement with him.

Tarakumar Choudhury.description: Latika Choudhury's husband, a railway engineer.

Dutta.description: A sub-inspector assisting Rakhal Sarkar in the investigation.

Ghose.description: Another sub-inspector involved in the investigation.

Nirupama Hotel.description: A westernised hotel in Calcutta where the murder takes place.

Rashbehari Avenue.description: A major road in Calcutta, location of Nirupama Hotel.

Gariahat Square.description: A well-known intersection in Calcutta, near the hotel.

Calcutta.description: The city (now Kolkata) where the story is set.

Beharampur.description: A town in West Bengal where Dr. Shobhona Roy practices.

Seva Sadan.description: An institution in Calcutta with which Dr. Roy is contracted.

Adampur.description: A locality in Patna, Bihar, listed as Rajkumar Basu's home address.

Patna.description: Capital city of Bihar, India, associated with the victim's alias.

Bihar.description: An Indian state, referenced as Rajkumar Basu's home state.

Bhagalpur.description: A city in Bihar, home of Shachitosh Sanyal.

Ganguram.description: A famous chain of sweet shops in Calcutta.

Orissa.description: Now Odisha, an Indian state, mentioned as Jagabandhu Patra's origin.

Benares.description: Also known as Varanasi, a city in Uttar Pradesh, India.

Port Commissioner's office.description: A government office in Calcutta where Shyamakanta Lahiri works.

Kalketu.description: The name of a newspaper whose archives Byomkesh consults.

Burdwan.description: A city in West Bengal, where Dr. Roy previously practiced.

Midnapore.description: A district in West Bengal, where Bhagaban Mohanti committed a crime.

India.description: The country in which all the events take place.

bed-tea.description: Morning tea served to guests in their rooms, a common practice in Indian hotels.

lungi.description: A traditional garment worn around the waist, common in South Asia.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

babu.description: A respectful term for a gentleman, often used as a suffix to names.

boarder.description: A person who rents a room in a hotel or boarding house.

sub-inspector.description: A rank in the Indian police force, below inspector.

tout.description: A person who solicits business or acts as an agent, often with a negative connotation in India.
